s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly progressive headache with a well-defined mass in the parietal bone
salient_findings: Mild headaches of several months’ duration
19-mm mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images with multiple internal hyperintense foci
key_facts: 65-year-old man
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus
Bronchial asthma
Mild headaches of several months’ duration
No focal neurologic deficits
Cranial MRI 4 years earlier showed no significant change in the identified lesion
Laboratory studies were normal
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a well-defined mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion centered in the diploic space with sparse but preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge
MRI showed the lesion to be isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion had multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images
Lesion had heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images and restricted diffusion

shortlist.label: Intraosseous metaplastic meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by identifying ossification and lipomatous tissue

shortlist.label: Osseous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to preserved trabecular architecture and sparse but preserved trabeculae

shortlist.label: Hyperplastic bone marrow
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to T1 hyperintense foci, but less likely due to other characteristics

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to well-defined mass in the parietal bone with sparse but preserved trabeculae

shortlist.label: Intraosseous lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible due to T1 hyperintense foci and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images

raw.rationale: The lesion's characteristics, such as being centered in the diploic space with preserved trabeculae, slight bony bulge, and internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images, along with heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images and restricted diffusion, are consistent with intraosseous metaplastic meningioma. The stability of the lesion over 4 years also supports a benign diagnosis like meningioma.

rejected.label: Osseous hemangioma
rejected.why: While osseous hemangioma could explain some imaging features, the specific combination of findings and the lack of typical 'honeycomb' or 'corduroy' appearance on imaging makes it less likely.

rejected.label: Hyperplastic bone marrow
rejected.why: Hyperplastic bone marrow could account for T1 hyperintense foci, but it does not fully explain the heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images, restricted diffusion, or the well-defined mass in the diploic space.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoma is typically a well-defined, dense bony lesion, which does not match the heterogeneous signal and internal hyperintense foci seen on MRI in this case.

rejected.label: Intraosseous lipoma
rejected.why: Intraosseous lipoma could explain some of the imaging features, especially the hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images, but the presence of heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images and restricted diffusion, along with the specific location and characteristics of the lesion, make intraosseous metaplastic meningioma a more comprehensive diagnosis.
